items.title: Pay 'Rechnung' for private Grundstücksregister entry
items.computation: The letter states a fixed calendar date for payment, '01.12.2026', rather than a period to be counted. 2026-12-01 is a Tuesday, not a weekend or NW public holiday, so no §193 BGB shift applies. The stated due date stands as written.

warnings: This document has the visual format of an invoice ('Rechnung', invoice number, due date, bank details) but the small print itself says 'Dieses Schreiben ist ein Angebot. Mit Ihrer Zahlung nehmen Sie es an; ein Vertrag kommt erst durch die Zahlung zustande' — i.e. no contract and no payment obligation exists yet; paying it would be the act of accepting an offer, not settling a debt.

The sender explicitly disclaims any connection to the official land registry: 'Die Eintragung erfolgt im privaten Verzeichnis des Absenders und steht in keinem Zusammenhang mit dem amtlichen Grundbuch.' This matches a well-known German scam pattern in which private companies send invoice-styled offers to property owners for a worthless private 'register' entry, trying to look like an official Grundbuchamt fee.
There is no legal obligation to pay this; the recommendation is not to pay and not to respond unless the person deliberately wants to purchase this private listing service.
No Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung (legal remedy instructions) is present, consistent with this being a private commercial offer rather than an official administrative act.
